primitives.name: Simultaneous Contrast Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The gray bars appear strongly colored by contrast, although, since they occupy as much space as the green bars, we are not deceived into believing that we see the former through a green medium.
primitives.assumptions: Perceptual contrast arises from lateral inhibition in retinal ganglion cells; observer is stationary under uniform illumination.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When foreground and background intensities approach equality (I_{\text{fg}} \approx I_{\text{bg}}), C_{\text{obs}} \to 0.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian model treats C_{\text{obs}} as likelihood ratio between two Gaussian-distributed intensity fields; GSE state transition uses C_{\text{obs}} as input to attention modulation.
layer2.telemetry: Color appearance shift measured via psychophysical thresholding of contrast discrimination.

primitives.name: Outline Tracing Interference
primitives.verbatim_quote: Why, then, if it is a true sensation due to physiological causes, and not an error of judgment, which causes the contrast, does the color disappear when the outlines of the gray scrap are traced, enabling us to recognize it as an independent object?
primitives.assumptions: Visual recognition activates top-down neural pathways that suppress bottom-up contrast signals.

layer2.mapping: GSI inference updates prior belief about object identity based on boundary cues; GSE applies this to update internal model of scene structure.
layer2.telemetry: Change in perceived contrast after tracing measured via repeated stimulus presentation with and without outline marking.

primitives.name: Retinal Excitation Modulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: To thoroughly guard against successive contrast, which so easily complicates the phenomena, we must carefully prevent all previous excitation of the retina by colored light.
primitives.assumptions: Retinal adaptation follows exponential decay; prior stimulation affects current response via temporal integration.

layer2.mapping: GSI models E_{\text{prev}} as prior distribution over sensory inputs; GSE uses M_{\text{mod}} to adjust sensory prediction error in hierarchical Bayesian networks.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal contrast sensitivity function derived from flicker detection thresholds at varying inter-stimulus intervals.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of simultaneous contrast operates through lateral inhibition within retinal ganglion cells, where adjacent regions of differing luminance generate antagonistic responses. This leads to apparent color shifts that persist even when spatial boundaries are defined. The interference from outline tracing suggests that object recognition modulates these physiological responses, indicating a dual pathway: one driven by raw intensity differences and another by cognitive interpretation. When outlines are drawn, the brain's object segmentation process alters the neural representation, effectively reducing the contrast signal. Retinal excitation history further complicates this by introducing temporal dependencies, where prior exposure to light modifies subsequent perception. These dynamics form a nonlinear system where contrast perception depends not only on absolute intensities but also on contextual and temporal factors. The failure mode occurs when these mechanisms interact unpredictably—such as when strong prior excitation masks new stimuli or when recognition fails to suppress residual contrast. Thus, the system exhibits both deterministic behavior under controlled conditions and stochastic variability under naturalistic variation.
